> Thanks for the heads up — I see the alert on our side too (NH-1472).
> Quick notes and immediate next steps: ...

I've pulled the live metrics. Short summary:
- Symptom: sharp 5xx spike peaking ~03:05 PST with corresponding 10–15s tail-latency.
- Root cause hypothesis (initial): Dedicated pool nh-prod-dedicated hit GPU capacity exhaustion while autoscaler attempted to add instances. Instance start latency (~3–6m cold start for some machine types) created a capacity gap.
- Amplifier: Nimble's orchestrator issued rapid retries (~1–3s intervals). Retries hit the front-end router and queue, increasing concurrency and causing request timeouts.

Immediate mitigations I pushed (03:35 PST):
1) Temporarily increased reserved capacity on the dedicated pool by +2 nodes (manual scale).
2) Adjusted autoscaler to more aggressive target (scale-up threshold -> 55% utilization).
3) Enabled short-term ingress throttling for NH project id to reduce new inflight requests while pool stabilizes.

Effects so far: error-rate down from 18% -> 6% over 8 minutes; latency reducing. Still monitoring.

Attachments: gpu-utilization-20270220.csv (minute-level), error-rate-dash-20270220.png (screenshot).

Notes for follow-up: need to discuss warm pool/predictive scaling and default client backoff guidance with Nimble. Also confirm whether any recent quantization/firmware changes coincided with the job.

Subject: Re: Severe 5xx/429 spikes impacting inference jobs — urgent

Diagnosis details (initial):
- Observed pattern: high concurrency, long-context requests (average seq len ~6k tokens) from NH batch jobs. These drive higher GPU memory and longer per-request execution time.
- Autoscaler interaction: scale-up triggers correctly fired but instance provisioning + runtime warm-up (LLM load + KV cache population) created a 3–7 minute window where effective capacity lagged demand.
- Retry amplification: client retries without jitter at short intervals (<=3s) — front-end queue depth spiked and front-end started returning 429/5xx due to exhausted worker threads.

Short-term remediation (done / in progress):
- Manual reserved capacity increase (+2 nodes) — done.
- Throttle ingress and enforce exponential backoff client-side guidance — applied on our router for NH.
- Temporarily lower max request-length for NH to reduce per-request GPU memory pressure (opt-in change; will coordinate with Nimble).

Longer term recommendations:
1) Warm pools for scheduled heavy jobs (predictive warm-up).
2) Predictive autoscale based on customer-scheduled jobs and historical profile.
3) Router-level per-tenant circuit breaker that sends 503 quickly when queue depth exceeds safe thresholds to avoid amplification.
4) Update customer SDKs and docs with backoff best-practices; consider server-side recommended backoff header.

I'd like to get sign-off to schedule a technical runbook session with Nimble next week and to produce a joint postmortem.

— Rishi
Head of Reliability
